chain.label: Pilot failed to ensure FSII added at fueling
chain.trigger: the pilot did not request that a fuel system icing inhibitor (FSII) be added

chain.label: Jet A fuel without anti-icing additive, water present
chain.trigger: All jet fuels contain trace amounts of water, and a FSII lowers the freezing point of water... to prevent the water from turning into ice crystals, which can block a fuel line or filter

caused_by.evidence: The fuel dispensed at the VCB self-service fueling island was not premixed with a FSII... no evidence to suggest that the pilot had used any other method to add a FSII

chain.label: Prolonged cruise at FL250 with -40 C outside air temperature
chain.trigger: The average total air temperature corrected for airspeed resulted in an average outside air temperature of... -40º C (at cruise altitude) for the accident flight leg

chain.label: Incomplete preflight; fuel not sampled and filter bypass indicator not checked at VCB
chain.trigger: The video showed no evidence that the pilot had sampled fuel from either of the underwing fuel tank drains or the fuel filter drain

chain.label: Ice accumulation in fuel system concentrated at airframe fuel filter
chain.trigger: the low fuel pressure state and the restricted fuel supply from the left tank during the accident flight were the result of an accumulation of ice in the fuel system with an initial concentrated amount of ice at the airframe fuel filter

caused_by.evidence: if the pilot had added a FSII to the fuel for the flights on the day of the accident, as required, the ice accumulation in the fuel system would have been avoided
a possible cause is the fuel filter blocked with ice crystals
he would have had an opportunity to detect whether ice crystals or water were present in the fuel and determine whether the fuel filter bypass indicator was extended

chain.label: Low fuel pressure state; boost pumps cycling and left-side fuel flow restricted
chain.trigger: About 1 hour 13 minutes into the flight (about 1323), both fuel boost pumps began cycling because of a low fuel pressure state

caused_by.evidence: postaccident testing clearly showed that ice accumulation in the fuel system (as a result of not adding a FSII) could degrade the performance of many fuel system components

chain.label: Left-wing-heavy lateral fuel imbalance growing beyond 1,300 pounds
chain.trigger: the fuel supplied to the airplane's engine was being drawn solely from the right fuel tank by the right fuel boost pump, and the left-wing-heavy fuel imbalance continued to increase

caused_by.evidence: the low fuel pressure state and a restricted flow of fuel from the left wing tank led to a left-wing-heavy fuel imbalance that exceeded 1,300 pounds

chain.label: Pilot continued toward Bozeman instead of landing as soon as practical after imbalance exceeded limits
chain.trigger: the pilot elected to continue to BZN and did not comply with the PC-12 AFM requirement to land the airplane as soon as practical when the maximum allowable fuel imbalance... had been exceeded

caused_by.evidence: About 1 hour 32 minutes into the flight, the fuel quantity indicator would have displayed a six-bar differential between the left and the right fuel tanks

chain.label: Pilot underestimated seriousness of the fuel indications based on prior uneventful flights
chain.trigger: the pilot underestimated the seriousness of the initial fuel imbalance indications because he had not experienced any adverse outcomes from ignoring similar indications during previous flights

caused_by.evidence: The pilot had likely downplayed the seriousness of the initial advisories because no adverse outcomes resulted from ignoring the advisories during the flight from REI to VCB

chain.label: Delayed diversion to distant Butte, bypassing closer suitable airports, into a confined mountain valley
chain.trigger: the pilot began to divert about 20 to 31 minutes after his attempt to restore fuel balance was unsuccessful, and he chose BTM even though several closer airports along the airplane's route of flight were available

caused_by.evidence: his eventual decision to divert to BTM likely resulted from his recognition of the magnitude of the increasing left-wing-heavy fuel imbalance situation
The pressure on the pilot to continue to BZN and delay diverting to an alternate airport until the fuel imbalance became extreme was likely self-induced

chain.label: High, fast, steep approach requiring abnormal descent rate and a sharp low-altitude left turn
chain.trigger: the airplane needed to descend 3,550 feet within 1.8 miles... which would result in a descent rate of 5,000 feet per minute... the airplane had entered a steep left turn at an estimated altitude of 300 feet agl

caused_by.evidence: the limited distance between the mountain peaks and the airport restricted the pilot's ability to maneuver the airplane during the descent
full RWD aileron trim and full ANL rudder trim, which is consistent with a forward sideslip to the right and a left-wing-down rolling moment

chain.label: Loss of control while maneuvering the left-wing-heavy airplane near the runway
chain.trigger: a loss of control while the pilot was maneuvering the left-wing-heavy airplane near the approach end of the runway

caused_by.evidence: the left rudder trim and fuel imbalance would continue to roll the airplane to the left unless the wheel was deflected to the right
the pilot did not maintain control of the airplane with the dynamic maneuvers during the final moments of the flight

chain.label: Airplane impacted terrain in a cemetery west of runway 33
chain.trigger: The airplane impacted the ground about 2,100 feet west of the runway 33 centerline

caused_by.evidence: the airplane roll to the left before entering a steep bank, pitching down, and impacting the ground

chain.label: Pilot and 13 passengers fatally injured; airplane destroyed by impact and postcrash fire
chain.trigger: The pilot and the 13 airplane passengers were fatally injured, and the airplane was substantially damaged by impact forces and a postcrash fire

caused_by.evidence: The Forensic Science Division of the Department of Justice in Missoula, Montana, assigned the cause of death for all of the airplane occupants as blunt force injuries
